the 3° alcohol that chromate cannot oxidize reacts fastest with the Lucas reagent.

Why the switch? Chromium(VI) compounds are toxic and cause cancer, and their waste needs special handling, so the teaching lab avoids them. Dichromate is still one of the most common oxidizing agents in chemistry, so know the chromate test and its orange-to-green color change for exams.

597191.old: Digestion of starch: in Experiment 13 – Enzymes you mix starch with amylase
597191.new:
Digestion of starch and sucrose: in Experiment 8 – Tests for Carbohydrates (Part E) you model digestion by heating starch and sucrose with dilute HCl. The acid hydrolyzes the glycosidic bonds, just as digestive enzymes do: the iodine test shows the starch is gone, and Benedict’s test turns positive because reducing sugars (glucose, and fructose from sucrose) appear. The tubes heated with water alone do not change.

In Experiment 13 – Enzymes you mix starch with amylase
597191.note: 13.3 In the Lab: digestion modeled by Exp 8 Part E acid hydrolysis
